newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth gets state nod on long distance.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth gets state nod on long distance.

text.p: BellSouth Corp said Thursday that South Carolina regulators had determined that the carrier had met key requirements needed so that the Baby Bell can offer long-distance service from the state.
BellSouth, as a result, said it plans to ask the Federal Communications Commission for permission to enter the long-distance market from South Carolina this fall.

The South Carolina Public Service Commission agreed that BellSouth had met a 14-point federal checklist that must be met before entry into the long-distance market, the carrier said. The checklist stems from last year's communications law.
The regulators' decision "demonstrates they support the interests of the citizens of our state," said Joe Anderson, president of BellSouth in South Carolina.

Any final clearance for BellSouth will rest with the FCC. The agency recently rejected SBC Communications Inc's application to offer long-distance service from Oklahoma, saying the carrier had not fully opened its market in the state to competitors.
